observation_summary: The BrentOptimizer algorithm fails to return the best point found during optimization, instead returning the last evaluated point, which may be worse than a previously encountered point.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a logic error in the optimization procedure where the algorithm fails to track or compare the best point found. This is a classic algorithmic correctness issue where the implementation of the optimization process is flawed, fitting the definition of Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'BrentOptimizer ... does not check that the point it is going to return is indeed the best one it has encountered. Indeed, the last evaluated point might be slightly worse than the one before last.'
The test failure 'Best point not reported' confirms the optimizer is not returning the optimal value found during its execution.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve initializing a variable to track the best point, the core issue is the logic of the optimization algorithm itself, not just a missing initialization.
The issue is not a missing validation of input parameters, but a failure in the internal logic of the optimization algorithm to correctly identify the best result.
